audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the packet chart and all seven content win[] rows read Brand, and the late row hedged with 'generally carries'.
audit.why: Brand's Q is 1050 range on an 8-second cooldown against Winds of War at 825 on 11 seconds and a 650-range Justice Punch; lane belongs to Brand at 52.48% over 484 games. What genuinely evens out is the two-item phase, where Hero's Entrance shields a whole team and Galio's magic resist blunts the burn.
audit.corrected: Brand on rows 0-5, even at two-plus items, with win[6] moved to Skill to match the full layer's existing 'Skill' and both whys rewritten to argue it.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text described Winds of War only as 'a slow skillshot with a long cooldown', and no spike anywhere carried a number.
audit.why: Winds of War is 11/10/9/8/7 against Brand's 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 Q — that specific gap is why Brand wins the poke war, and Hero's Entrance at 180 seconds rank 1 is why his teamfight spike is a timer you can track.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into spikes[0].text, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[3] and spikes[2].text both treat Shield of Durand as a spell shield that 'blocks a key spell'. Colossal Smash's auto reset and the fact that Justice Punch can land between you and safety were both absent.
audit.why: Riot's Shield of Durand text describes a slow-moving defensive charge that taunts and damages nearby enemies on release, at 275 range on 18 seconds at rank 1 — nothing about blocking a spell. Brand has no dash, so a Justice Punch that arrives behind him takes his retreat away and Flash is the only answer. Colossal Smash resets his auto for bonus area damage, which is what actually punishes an extended trade at his range.
audit.corrected: Shield-block claim removed from both fields; auto reset stated in dontsFull[1].d; the retreat problem stated in dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and the packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'.
audit.why: Justice Punch at 11 seconds is the only engage he owns; while it is down there is no fight he can start.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch 11s, Shield of Durand 275 range, Winds of War 11s and Hero's Entrance 180s now stated, phrased as when to step up.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, dontsFull[1].d did not match its title, and whys[6] hedged with 'generally'.
audit.why: A bullet body must explain its own title, and a hedge says nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch carries a derived 'terrain' flag and Brand's W carries one too.
audit.why: Riot's descriptions are a charge-and-knockup and a delayed area damage zone respectively. Neither creates terrain; both flags are parsing misfires.
audit.corrected: No terrain claim written for either. The retreat-cutting point was stated as the dash landing behind you, which the description does support.

edits.before: Late Brand is a teamfight detonator: spread Blaze, R the clump, and watch three health bars argue with physics.
edits.after: Late reads even: you detonate the clump, but Hero's Entrance shields his whole side and knocks you off it.

edits.before: His tankiness and teamfight-ultimate give him a genuine tool to offset your lead in group fights, though your lane advantage still generally carries.
edits.after: 2+ items: his magic resist and a Hero's Entrance that shields the whole team offset your burst, so late fights read even rather than yours.

edits.before: You keep winning trades cleanly as his damage output stays well below yours.
edits.after: Level 3 E-Q stuns him mid-approach, and Justice Punch is 11s if he misses.

edits.before: Poke advantage holds steady through level 5 with no meaningful counter from his kit.
edits.after: Your rotation out-damages a tornado on an 11-second cooldown all the way to level 5.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - E-Q stun package spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 and reaches 650 — while it is down he has no engage, so that is when you step up. - Shield of Durand taunts from only 275. - Winds of War is 11s, Hero's Entrance 180s.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Galio wins by Justice Punching through your minions, taunting you at 275 range, and shielding his team through your burn.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Justice Punch is his only engage, 11 seconds at rank 1 — commit on its downtime, never into it.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Justice Punch dashes 650 and knocks up the first champion it reaches — pillar the narrow ground and he pays to arrive on you.

edits.before: Your stun only exists on ablaze targets — a Q thrown at a clean health bar is the most expensive miss in your kit.
edits.after: Colossal Smash resets his auto for bonus area damage, so an extended trade at his range is him hitting you for free.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance drops a magic shield on everyone at the landing spot, so a Sear spent into that shield buys you nothing.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by pricing the approach — he crosses 650 units of pillar to reach taunt range, and Blaze stacks the whole way in.

edits.before: Ahead, scorch the map: rotation-poke Galio off every wave, stun the answers, and R every river clump — fed Brand turns skirmishes into actuarial tables.
edits.after: Ahead, tax the approach: shove with W-E, punish every Justice Punch whiff with E-Q, and roam the moment his 180-second ultimate is spent.

edits.before: Galio's Winds of War poke is a slow skillshot with a long cooldown, so your Q lands more consistently and your passive stacking snowballs faster than his early trade potential.
edits.after: Winds of War is an 11-second cooldown at rank 1 against your 8-second Q, so you land more poke per wave and Blaze stacks faster than anything his early trades can answer.

edits.before: Liandry's burn punishes his Shield of Durand channel — he has to stand still to get full value from the spell shield, and your DoT keeps ticking through it once it expires.
edits.after: Liandry's burn punishes the Shield of Durand charge — he crawls while holding it and still has to reach 275 range to taunt, so the burn ticks through his entire approach.

edits.before: Use Shield of Durand to block a key spell in a skirmish
edits.after: Charge Shield of Durand and taunt you at its 275 range

notes: Full-layer sides were 'Skill' on every row against an all-Brand packet chart, an all-Brand content chart and a 52.48% win rate; moved to Brand for rows 0-5. Row 6 was already 'Skill' on the full layer, so the twin edit is win[6] Brand to Skill, with both whys rewritten to argue the even verdict. The page treated Shield of Durand as a spell shield in two places; Riot's text says only that it charges slowly and taunts nearby enemies on release, so the blocking claim was removed rather than restated. Justice Punch's derived 'terrain' flag and Brand's W 'terrain' flag both contradict their descriptions and were not used.
